claims.text: The baseline no-show charge fails on the driver's own record. The trip was terminated by the DRIVER at 15:18:40 with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires one of RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is expressly excluded: it is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, and the clause directs that such a trip is decided under POL-NS-03. One broken limb is enough to defeat the charge - the $4.00 is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

The driver never entered the pickup geofence. For LARGE_VENUE the arrival radius is 120 m; the driver's own trace shows qualifying_fix_count 0 and a closest approach of 284.95 m from the pin, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes preceding cancellation. Under POL-NS-02 that means the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund. I disclose that EV-GPS-00206 is tagged IMPAIRED by the pre-pass at weight 0.8 with issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE: the tag is about sampling cadence only, the assessor records no gap at all (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), 52 fixes across the window and the rider track present, so it meets none of POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d) and the measured 284.95 m minimum stands at full value.

On the wrong-face facts POL-NS-03 requires the refund. The driver's closest approach was 284.95 m from the pin - outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets as the whole test - and both accounts agree he was waiting at the HarbourFront kerb rather than at Lobby L: the driver states 'the map put me at the HarbourFront kerb. I waited almost seven minutes,' which matches the trip record's wait_time_min of 6.6, and the rider states the pin dropped him at Lobby L. POL-NS-03 treats an honest mispickup at the wrong face of the same venue as no one's fault and refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. If the judge prefers to read the trace as not establishing a qualifying 400 m dwell, the case simply falls back to POL-NS-02, which mandates the same full refund on the total absence of qualifying in-radius fixes. EV-GPS-00206 is cited at its impaired weight of 0.8 (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE), which affects cadence only and not the distance figure.

Independently of arrival, the waiting period was never served. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds - longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0, run_count 0 - against a 300 second minimum for LARGE_VENUE, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full on a shortfall, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The accumulation route in limb (i) is unavailable because no traffic advisory covers these kerbs at all: I cite the absence of EV-ADVIS-00206-01 rather than asserting it, so there is no present and populated advisory that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and nothing reduces the required minimum. EV-GPS-00206 is disclosed at weight 0.8 with issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE - a cadence tag that leaves this 0-second dwell measurement untouched.

I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it. The chat log holds only two SYSTEM notifications - 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived' - and no message from the rider, so limb (a), which requires a rider locating or coordinating message, is not met and that clause is unavailable on this record. What the rider's own track does establish is that the rider was standing at the pin the entire time: 31 fixes, every one stationary, never more than 22.5 m from the pickup pin and averaging 15.4 m, well inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE (31 of 31 fixes qualifying). The failure was on the driver's side of the kerb, not the rider's. EV-GPS-00206 is disclosed at its impaired weight of 0.8, issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, which does not touch the rider track's completeness or its stationary distances.

The cost of this mispickup should land on the platform, never on the rider. POL-NS-03 allocates fault from the chat log alone, and the chat log carries no sub-location from either party - neither the rider nor the driver named a block, entrance, tower or bay. That engages POL-NS-03 limb (ii): with 4 registered pickup points at this venue, the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, $2.00 of the $4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. Whichever way the arrival question is resolved, the rider's $4.00 does not fund the outcome.

The sum in dispute is exactly $4.00 and it is wholly the cancellation-fee line: fare_breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The figure reconciles with the schedule - the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of $4.00 against the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of $4.00, so the greater-of rule yields $4.00 - and there is no fare-integrity defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) describes. Under POL-GEN-03, FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned, and the rider is the filing party; a full refund therefore returns the whole $4.00 and leaves the rider carrying none of the disputed charge.

This case should be decided on the money, not held. None of POL-NS-09's triggers is present: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limbs (c) and (d) are out on the rider side; driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far below the 4 that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires, so limb (d) is out on the driver side too; and the only impairment in the bundle is schema-level - EV-GPS-00206's LOW_SAMPLE_RATE tag fails every limb of POL-NS-08 (no gap over 120 s, 52 fixes in the window, rider track present), so limb (e) is not engaged. Under POL-GEN-02 the deciding facts are also carried by EV-TRIP-00206 at weight 1.0. ESCALATE would hold the $4.00 rather than return it; the record supports FULL_REFUND of it.

claims.text: Honest position on the anchor clause: the cancellation reason code on this trip is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The baseline chargeable no-show therefore cannot be made out on this record, and the driver does not claim the 80 percent payout of SGD 3.20 under POL-NS-07 — that clause requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not. The fee falls to be decided, as POL-NS-01 itself directs, under POL-NS-03.

The arrival radius was never entered: the driver's qualifying_fix_count is 0 against the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, and the closest recorded approach on the trace is 284.95 m. That fails POL-NS-01 limb (b) via POL-NS-02 — but POL-NS-02 expressly yields where the driver was nonetheless stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, which is this trace. The trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8; the impairment is disclosed and does not disturb the number: 52 fixes span the window at an 18 s median cadence with a largest interval of 26 s, inside POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 s gap and 6-fix thresholds, so neither limb of that defect bites.

This is a wrong-approach case on POL-NS-03's own arithmetic. The driver's stationary hold sits at a minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m from the pin — outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the clause's 400 m ceiling — and he held for the required dwell: the trip record logs a 6.6 minute wait, arrival at 15:12:05 to cancellation at 15:18:40, i.e. 395 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum. His stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h; the large distances elsewhere on the trace (max 5,480.89 m) belong to the 6.8 km approach, not the hold. The GPS trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed, and 52 fixes over the window are sufficient to carry this finding.

Fault under POL-NS-03 is allocated to pin ambiguity, not to either party. The chat log contains no message from either side naming a sub-location — only two SYSTEM notifications, 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' at 15:03:31 and 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:12:06 — and the trip record shows four registered pickup points at this LARGE_VENUE zone. Under POL-NS-03(ii) that is pin ambiguity rather than party fault, and the driver is entitled to a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee: SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

The rider was waiting at the pin, so this is a genuine two-party mislocation rather than a rider who never appeared: her own track places her device between 7.57 m and 22.50 m of the pin across all 31 of her fixes, every one of them inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius. Both parties were present at the venue, neither named a sub-location, and the driver's vehicle could not be brought inside a 120 m radius he never entered. That is exactly the fact pattern POL-NS-03 was written for: the fee goes back and the driver's cost is met from the platform. GPS trace impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8, disclosed.

POL-NS-04 cannot be used to strip the driver of any cost-sharing. Limb (a) requires a rider message sent during the waiting window whose content locates or coordinates, and the chat log holds no rider message at all — its only two entries are SYSTEM notifications, one of them the arrival notice itself. With limb (a) unmet the clause never opens, whatever limb (c) would have shown about rider position, and the fault allocation stays with POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not turn this into a false-arrival refund with a referral against the driver. The clause bites only where the arrival timestamp places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at 15 km/h or more; the trace's minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m sits inside that 300 m line and the stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h, so no false marker is shown, and the clause's own closing sentence sends this driver — stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival — to POL-NS-03. The GPS trace is impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed; the trace nonetheless records the position the finding rests on.

Nothing withholds the payment and nothing requires escalation. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check needs both limbs — 4 or more no-show terminations in 30 days AND a rate above 0.08 — and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 187, a rate of 0.005; neither limb trips, so the payment is not withheld and no POL-NS-09(d) referral arises. The POL-NS-09(c) counterparty counts are 0 on both profiles and rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 0.8 and 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is 1.0 and confidence stays above the 0.70 floor: this case can and should be decided on its merits today.

The amount the driver's entitlement is computed on is sound. The SGD 4.00 ledger line matches fee_schedule.resolution_rule for this trip: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). There is accordingly no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the 50 percent goodwill resolves to SGD 2.00 on a fully reconciled SGD 4.00 base.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0; no advisory covers these kerbs in this window. The driver does not assert POL-NS-06(i) interval-summing — a MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact would be improper. He does not need it: his case rests on POL-NS-03's 400 m test and the recorded dwell, which are decidable from the coordinates alone without any advisory.

For completeness on the rider's refund, which the driver does not contest: the effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a 300 second shortfall, so the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full under POL-NS-06. The driver accepts that outcome; the live question the driver argues is the separate, platform-funded goodwill of SGD 2.00 under POL-NS-03(ii), which is a payment by the platform and is never netted against the rider's refund.

ruling.explanation:
This is a wrong-kerb pickup, not a no-show, and the money follows that finding.

To the rider: the S$4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to you in full. You were waiting where the app pinned you — your own device track holds you between about 8 and 23 metres of the Lobby L pin for the entire wait, well inside the 150-metre rider-presence radius for a large venue — and the charge cannot stand. To the driver: you are not being blamed. Your trace shows you holding station about 285 metres away at the HarbourFront kerb, outside the 120-metre arrival radius but inside the 400-metre limit POL-NS-03 sets, and the app's map put you there. Because neither of you named a sub-location in the in-app chat (it holds only two system messages) and this venue has four registered pickup points, POL-NS-03(ii) treats this as pin ambiguity rather than fault and gives you a platform-funded goodwill payment of half the fee — S$2.00 — charged to the platform and never taken from the rider. The refund and your goodwill are independent and are not netted.

How I got there. POL-NS-01, the baseline no-show clause, needs all four of its conditions. Condition (b) fails: no GPS fix of yours falls inside the 120-metre arrival radius (qualifying_fix_count 0). Condition (d) fails: the trip was closed with DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which the clause expressly excludes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. POL-NS-02 would itself refund the fee on the total absence of an in-radius fix, but it yields to POL-NS-03 where the driver was stationary for the required dwell within 400 metres, and that is what the trace shows — a hold of roughly 400 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, at a closest recorded approach of 284.95 metres and 0.0 km/h. POL-NS-03 therefore governs: it refunds the S$4.00 and, on limb (ii), awards the S$2.00 goodwill.

On the other arguments. I accept both sides' reading that POL-NS-01 fails and the case falls to POL-NS-03, and both sides' reading that POL-NS-04 does not apply — the chat log carries no rider coordinating message, so limb (a) never opens and the fault allocation stays with POL-NS-03. POL-NS-05 does not bite either: the 284.95-metre closest approach is inside the 300-metre false-marker line and the stationary fixes read 0.0 km/h, so no false-arrival record arises and the clause's own closing sentence sends this driver, stationary within 300 m but outside the radius, to POL-NS-03. On POL-NS-07, the anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 187 completed trips, a rate of 0.005, against the thresholds of 4 and 0.08), so nothing is withheld and no POL-NS-09 escalation is engaged; the S$2.00 here is the POL-NS-03(ii) platform goodwill, not the 80 per cent payout, which requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full and it is not. No POL-NS-09 trigger is present: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence (the trip record's 6.6-minute wait and the trace's ~400-second hold agree), the counterparty counts are 0 on both profiles, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d).

On confidence. The deciding position fact is carried by the GPS trace EV-GPS-00206, which the pre-pass tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.8 for LOW_SAMPLE_RATE (median 18-second cadence). I do not accept the suggestion that the cap is 1.0: the trip record does not independently place the vehicle, so the deciding fact rests on the 0.8 trace alone. That impairment is schema-level only and fails every limb of POL-NS-08 — the largest interval is 26 seconds against the 120-second gap threshold, there are 52 fixes against the 6-fix threshold, the rider track is present, and the S$4.00 fare reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule (the greater of the LARGE_VENUE S$4.00 and the RYDE_X S$4.00) — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the 284.95-metre figure stands at full value. Both of you were at the same venue at different kerbs, and neither is at fault. Here is how the case is decided.

THE $4.00 CHARGE DOES NOT STAND. POL-NS-01 requires all four limbs. The arrival limbs fail too: the driver's trace never enters the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius (qualifying in-geofence fixes 0, closest recorded approach 284.95 m) and the in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum. The cancellation fee is therefore refunded to the rider in full: SGD 4.00.

THIS IS A WRONG-ENTRANCE CASE UNDER POL-NS-03. The driver was stationary for the required dwell at a point outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but inside the clause's 400 m ceiling (284.95 m), which is why POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03 here. The fee goes back to the rider and the driver's cost is met by the platform. On fault allocation under POL-NS-03(ii): the chat log holds only two SYSTEM notifications and no sub-location from either side, and the trip record shows four registered pickup points at this LARGE_VENUE zone. The mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee: SGD 2.00. It is charged to the platform, never recovered from the rider, and is not netted against the rider's refund.

EVIDENCE WEIGHT. EV-GPS-00206 is tagged IMPAIRED by the pre-pass at weight 0.8 for LOW_SAMPLE_RATE (median 18 s against a nominal 10 s cadence). That is a schema-level cadence tag only: the trace has no gap at all (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), 52 fixes across the window and the rider track present, so it meets none of POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d) and the positions it records stand at full value. Because the refund's deciding fact — the driver's position — is carried by that trace at weight 0.8, my confidence is capped at 0.8 under POL-GEN-02(2). That is above the 0.70 floor, so the case is decided, not escalated.

POINTS RAISED AND ANSWERED. (1) POL-NS-04 does not open: limb (a) needs a locating or coordinating rider message and the chat log contains none. (2) POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the driver's closest approach, 284.95 m, is inside the 300 m line and his stationary fixes read 0.0 km/h, so the arrival marker is not false and no false-arrival referral arises. (3) The rider was at the pin: her own track places her 7.57–22.50 m from the pin across all 31 fixes, every one inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, so this was a genuine two-party mislocation and not an absent rider. (4) No escalation: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check needs both 4 or more no-show terminations in 30 days and a rate above 0.08, and the driver shows 1 against 187 completed trips (rate 0.005); POL-NS-09(c) counterparty counts are 0 on both profiles, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and the only impairment in the bundle is schema-level, so POL-NS-09(a)–(e) are all out. (5) The SGD 4.00 line is sound: it reconciles with the greater-of rule for the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

OUTCOME. Rider refunded SGD 4.00; driver receives SGD 2.00 in platform-funded goodwill.

POL-NS-03 treats an honest mispickup at the wrong face of the same venue as no one's fault and refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. If the judge prefers to read the trace as not establishing a qualifying 400 m dwell, the case simply falls back to POL-NS-02, which mandates the same full refund on the total absence of qualifying in-radius fixes. EV-GPS-00206 is cited at its impaired weight of 0.8 (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE), which affects cadence only and not the distance figure.

Independently of arrival, the waiting period was never served. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds - longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0, run_count 0 - against a 300 second minimum for LARGE_VENUE, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full on a shortfall, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The accumulation route in limb (i) is unavailable because no traffic advisory covers these kerbs at all: I cite the absence of EV-ADVIS-00206-01 rather than asserting it, so there is no present and populated advisory that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and nothing reduces the required minimum. EV-GPS-00206 is disclosed at weight 0.8 with issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE - a cadence tag that leaves this 0-second dwell measurement untouched.

ledger.claim: I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it. The chat log holds only two SYSTEM notifications - 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived' - and no message from the rider, so limb (a), which requires a rider locating or coordinating message, is not met and that clause is unavailable on this record. What the rider's own track does establish is that the rider was standing at the pin the entire time: 31 fixes, every one stationary, never more than 22.5 m from the pickup pin and averaging 15.4 m, well inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE (31 of 31 fixes qualifying). The failure was on the driver's side of the kerb, not the rider's. EV-GPS-00206 is disclosed at its impaired weight of 0.8, issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, which does not touch the rider track's completeness or its stationary distances.

The cost of this mispickup should land on the platform, never on the rider. POL-NS-03 allocates fault from the chat log alone, and the chat log carries no sub-location from either party - neither the rider nor the driver named a block, entrance, tower or bay. That engages POL-NS-03 limb (ii): with 4 registered pickup points at this venue, the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, $2.00 of the $4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. Whichever way the arrival question is resolved, the rider's $4.00 does not fund the outcome.

The sum in dispute is exactly $4.00 and it is wholly the cancellation-fee line: fare_breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The figure reconciles with the schedule - the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of $4.00 against the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of $4.00, so the greater-of rule yields $4.00 - and there is no fare-integrity defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) describes. Under POL-GEN-03, FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned, and the rider is the filing party; a full refund therefore returns the whole $4.00 and leaves the rider carrying none of the disputed charge.

This case should be decided on the money, not held. None of POL-NS-09's triggers is present: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limbs (c) and (d) are out on the rider side; driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far below the 4 that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires, so limb (d) is out on the driver side too; and the only impairment in the bundle is schema-level - EV-GPS-00206's LOW_SAMPLE_RATE tag fails every limb of POL-NS-08 (no gap over 120 s, 52 fixes in the window, rider track present), so limb (e) is not engaged. Under POL-GEN-02 the deciding facts are also carried by EV-TRIP-00206 at weight 1.0. ESCALATE would hold the $4.00 rather than return it; the record supports FULL_REFUND of it.

Honest position on the anchor clause: the cancellation reason code on this trip is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The baseline chargeable no-show therefore cannot be made out on this record, and the driver does not claim the 80 percent payout of SGD 3.20 under POL-NS-07 — that clause requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not. The fee falls to be decided, as POL-NS-01 itself directs, under POL-NS-03.

The arrival radius was never entered: the driver's qualifying_fix_count is 0 against the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, and the closest recorded approach on the trace is 284.95 m. That fails POL-NS-01 limb (b) via POL-NS-02 — but POL-NS-02 expressly yields where the driver was nonetheless stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, which is this trace. The trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8; the impairment is disclosed and does not disturb the number: 52 fixes span the window at an 18 s median cadence with a largest interval of 26 s, inside POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 s gap and 6-fix thresholds, so neither limb of that defect bites.

This is a wrong-approach case on POL-NS-03's own arithmetic. The driver's stationary hold sits at a minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m from the pin — outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the clause's 400 m ceiling — and he held for the required dwell: the trip record logs a 6.6 minute wait, arrival at 15:12:05 to cancellation at 15:18:40, i.e. 395 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum. His stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h; the large distances elsewhere on the trace (max 5,480.89 m) belong to the 6.8 km approach, not the hold. The GPS trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed, and 52 fixes over the window are sufficient to carry this finding.

Fault under POL-NS-03 is allocated to pin ambiguity, not to either party. The chat log contains no message from either side naming a sub-location — only two SYSTEM notifications, 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' at 15:03:31 and 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:12:06 — and the trip record shows four registered pickup points at this LARGE_VENUE zone. Under POL-NS-03(ii) that is pin ambiguity rather than party fault, and the driver is entitled to a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee: SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

The rider was waiting at the pin, so this is a genuine two-party mislocation rather than a rider who never appeared: her own track places her device between 7.57 m and 22.50 m of the pin across all 31 of her fixes, every one of them inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius. Both parties were present at the venue, neither named a sub-location, and the driver's vehicle could not be brought inside a 120 m radius he never entered. That is exactly the fact pattern POL-NS-03 was written for: the fee goes back and the driver's cost is met from the platform. GPS trace impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8, disclosed.

POL-NS-04 cannot be used to strip the driver of any cost-sharing. Limb (a) requires a rider message sent during the waiting window whose content locates or coordinates, and the chat log holds no rider message at all — its only two entries are SYSTEM notifications, one of them the arrival notice itself. With limb (a) unmet the clause never opens, whatever limb (c) would have shown about rider position, and the fault allocation stays with POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not turn this into a false-arrival refund with a referral against the driver. The clause bites only where the arrival timestamp places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at 15 km/h or more; the trace's minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m sits inside that 300 m line and the stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h, so no false marker is shown, and the clause's own closing sentence sends this driver — stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival — to POL-NS-03. The GPS trace is impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed; the trace nonetheless records the position the finding rests on.

Nothing withholds the payment and nothing requires escalation. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check needs both limbs — 4 or more no-show terminations in 30 days AND a rate above 0.08 — and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 187, a rate of 0.005; neither limb trips, so the payment is not withheld and no POL-NS-09(d) referral arises. The POL-NS-09(c) counterparty counts are 0 on both profiles and rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 0.8 and 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is 1.0 and confidence stays above the 0.70 floor: this case can and should be decided on its merits today.

The amount the driver's entitlement is computed on is sound. The SGD 4.00 ledger line matches fee_schedule.resolution_rule for this trip: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). There is accordingly no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the 50 percent goodwill resolves to SGD 2.00 on a fully reconciled SGD 4.00 base.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0; no advisory covers these kerbs in this window. The driver does not assert POL-NS-06(i) interval-summing — a MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact would be improper. He does not need it: his case rests on POL-NS-03's 400 m test and the recorded dwell, which are decidable from the coordinates alone without any advisory.
